title: Review: Impulse and momentum with calculus; Rotational kinematics; Torque; Moment of inertia; · part 1 of 1; Moments and static equilibrium; Newton's second law for rotation
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics C: Mechanics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: R04-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; R03-calc-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; R01-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; R02-1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: R01-1#N.7, R03-1#N.11, R03-calc-1#N.9, R04-1#N.8b, R03-calc-1#N.10, D08-1#N.9, NEW-momentum-calc-1#N.10, R01-1#N.5b, R02-1#N.5b, R03-1#N.2, R03-calc-1#N.3, R04-1#N.5b. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Angular acceleration
items.clue: Symbol α: equal to the net turning effect on a body divided by its I.

items.label: Rotational inertia
items.clue: Quantity found for a solid by adding r² dm over every tiny piece of it.

items.label: Angular displacement
items.clue: Symbol Δθ: how far a body has turned about an axis, final θ minus initial θ.

items.label: Torque
items.clue: Turning effect of a force about an axis, in N m; greatest when the force is at 90° to r.

questions.stem: A light string is wrapped around a pulley of radius 0.0600 m that turns on a fixed axle. The string is pulled so that it unwinds without slipping while the pulley turns through 20.0 rad. What length of string unwinds from the pulley?

Two thin rods, X and Y, have the same mass and length. In rod X most of the mass is concentrated equally near the two ends; in rod Y most of the mass is concentrated near the middle. Each rod can rotate about an axis through its midpoint, perpendicular to the rod. Which claim about the rods' rotational inertias about these axes is correct?

options.text: Rod X's is greater, because more of its mass is far from the axis
Rod Y's is greater, because rod X's end masses give it more leverage
They are equal, because the rods have the same mass and length
It depends on where each rod is pushed, not on the rods alone

questions.stem: A uniform solid sphere of mass M and radius R has rotational inertia (2/5)MR² about an axis through its centre. It is fixed to the end of a light rod whose other end is at a pivot; the rod meets the sphere's surface, and the sphere's centre is a distance 2R from the pivot. What is the rotational inertia of the system about an axis through the pivot, perpendicular to the rod?

Two identical uniform pucks rest on a horizontal surface with negligible friction. A string is tied to a peg at the centre of puck 1, and a string is wrapped many times around the rim of puck 2. Each string is pulled horizontally with the same constant force F; puck 2's string unwinds as puck 2 spins. How do the accelerations of the pucks' centres of mass compare while the strings are pulled?

options.text: Puck 1's is greater, since puck 2 uses some of F to spin.
Puck 1's equals puck 2's: each resultant force is F.
Puck 2's is greater, since its string is pulled farther.
Puck 2's is zero, since F makes puck 2 spin instead.

questions.stem: A uniform disc of mass M and radius R rotates about an axis through its centre, perpendicular to its face. The axis is moved, parallel to itself, to a point on the disc's rim. By what factor does the disc's rotational inertia change?

An electric fan is switched on, and after a few seconds its blades turn at a constant angular velocity. Which statement about the torques exerted on the blades while they turn at this constant angular velocity is correct?

options.text: The motor's torque is balanced by the opposing torques.
The motor's torque exceeds the torques that oppose the rotation.
The net torque is not zero, since each point on a blade accelerates.
No torques are exerted, since the blades are in equilibrium.

questions.stem: A hose sends water horizontally at 2.0 kg s⁻¹ and 15 m s⁻¹ against a vertical wall. The water stops at the wall and runs straight down it. What is the magnitude of the horizontal force the water exerts on the wall? Use g = 10 m s⁻².
questions.explanation: F = v dm/dt = (15 m s⁻¹)(2.0 kg s⁻¹) = 30 N. Each second the wall takes 30 kg m s⁻¹ of horizontal momentum from the water, so the water pushes on the wall with 30 N.

questions.stem: Two identical fans, X and Y, start from rest. Each speeds up with constant angular acceleration until it reaches the same final angular velocity. The angular acceleration of fan X is twice that of fan Y. What is the ratio Δθ_X/Δθ_Y of the angles through which the fans turn while speeding up?

A rod of length 0.60 m can rotate about an axle through one end. A string is attached to the rod 0.40 m from the axle and pulls on it with a force of 50 N directed at 37° to the rod. What is the magnitude of the torque exerted on the rod by the string's force about the axle? Use sin 37° = 0.60 and cos 37° = 0.80.
A bicycle wheel can rotate about its axle. Which change would increase the wheel's rotational inertia about the axle?

options.text: Moving some of its mass from the rim in towards the hub
Spinning the wheel at a faster rate about the same axle
Pushing on the rim, rather than near the hub, to turn it
Moving some of its mass from the hub out to the rim

questions.stem: A thin uniform rod of mass 2.0 kg and length 1.2 m rotates about an axis perpendicular to the rod through a point 0.30 m from one end. Using I = ∫ r² dm, what is the rod's rotational inertia about this axis?

A solid disc of radius 0.50 m and rotational inertia 0.25 kg m² turns on a fixed axle. A string wrapped around its rim is pulled with a constant force of 2.0 N, tangent to the rim, in the sense in which the disc is turning. Friction at the axle exerts a constant torque of 0.25 N m that opposes the rotation. What is the magnitude of the disc's angular acceleration?
